topics.topic: Canonical ServiceExit enumeration member names versus lowercase values
questions: Are `start_failed`, `served` and `server_failed` member names, as the context says, or values of the `START_FAILED`, `SERVED` and `SERVER_FAILED` members, as A8 says?
Are `start_failed`, `served` and `server_failed` the enumeration member names, as this passage says, or are they values of the `START_FAILED`, `SERVED` and `SERVER_FAILED` members, as A8 says?
Name each member by its generated member name beside `= models.ServiceExit`, with the lowercase value only as an optional supplement.

quotes:
`ServiceExit` is the way the service process ends, which chooses its exit status; it is an enumeration of the
process, not a model of this state. Its members are exactly `start_failed`, `served` and `server_failed`; A8
decides what each means and its status.
judgement.why: The passage names the enumeration members only by their lowercase values instead of their generated member names.

topics.topic: Events and errors that count as post-boundary ServiceExit failures
questions: What exact events count as a “failure” after the boundary and therefore override an otherwise clean signal shutdown?

What exactly counts as a failure for ServiceExit classification: only an uncaught exception or nonzero termination, any raised exception even if caught, a logged error, a failed cleanup task, or some other defined condition?
What exactly counts as a failure after the boundary, including cleanup, logging, telemetry, signal-handler, task-cancellation, and process-exit errors?

quotes: run_service: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call load_runtime_settings, then load_config with those settings, then read_token with the credential_file of the settings as a Path, then the imported create_app with that context and token, in that order, and serve the application with the imported uvicorn on the host of the imported BIND_HOST constant and the port of the settings, trusting no forwarded or proxy header. It MUST return the status of the row of the imported EXIT_STATUSES constant for the member of = models.ServiceExit the way the process ends: the START_FAILED member when any step or a signal ends it before the web server listens, after writing one line naming the failed step to standard error and never the token; the SERVED member when its web server returns after a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and the SERVER_FAILED member for any other end after the web server has begun listening.
judgement.why: The later service note classifies the observable way the process ends: a clean signal-stopped server return is SERVED, while any other post-listening end is SERVER_FAILED.

topics.topic: Authoritative event that establishes the ServiceExit listening boundary
questions: Which exact web-server event or API report establishes the boundary, and does the report alone establish it or must socket acceptance be independently verified?
Which concrete event is authoritative when the server's startup-complete report and the socket becoming able to accept connections are not observably simultaneous?

quotes:
The service has begun listening once its web server reports
its startup complete, its socket accepting connections; that report is the boundary.
judgement.why: The startup-complete report itself is expressly the authoritative boundary.

topics.topic: Classification and ordering of termination events concurrent with the listening boundary
questions: How is the outcome chosen when the startup-boundary report and a terminating signal or shutdown are concurrent, with no defined ordering between them?
How is an end, signal, or failure occurring at the boundary itself classified, since the rules cover only before and after it?

quotes:
= models.ServiceExit
is START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before that boundary, whatever ends it, a signal
included; SERVED, value `served`: after it, a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way, a failure during or after the shutdown of a stopped server included, so any
failure after the boundary outranks the signal.
judgement.divergence: One implementation orders the startup-complete report first and returns SERVED/status 0; another orders the terminating signal first and returns START_FAILED/status 1, which the process supervisor observes.
judgement.why: The rules classify events before and after the boundary but give no ordering rule for a boundary report concurrent with termination.

witness.initial: The web server is completing startup while the process can receive a terminating signal.
events: The web server reports startup complete.
The process receives SIGTERM concurrently with that report and the web server returns without an error.
outcomes: The report is ordered first, so the outcome is SERVED and the status is 0.
The signal is ordered first, so the outcome is START_FAILED and the status is 1.
basis:
The service has begun listening once its web server reports
its startup complete, its socket accepting connections; that report is the boundary.

= models.ServiceExit
is START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before that boundary, whatever ends it, a signal
included; SERVED, value `served`: after it, a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way, a failure during or after the shutdown of a stopped server included, so any
failure after the boundary outranks the signal.

topics.topic: Source, representation, precision, and clock-read policy for PublicationMark.marked_at
questions: Which authority supplies the fresh instant written to `PublicationMark.marked_at`, and in which datetime representation is it passed and stored?
How many clock readings may the first mark operation and a replay take, and which reading supplies `marked_at` if an operation reads more than once?
What source supplies `marked_at`, what datetime representation and precision are stored, and how many clock readings does one mark operation take?

judgement.why: P2 judged the same source, representation, sampling point and clock-read-count questions, and the relevant A7 passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: How PublicationMark.marked_at is sourced, represented, sampled, and clock-read
quotes:
1. The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

2. Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.

- INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
precedent.why: The clock source, representation, reading point and Required tests passage are unchanged from the closed State 2, and the credential/environment-setting changes did not make this topic matter.

topics.topic: Classification when a signal arrives before the boundary but stops the server afterward
questions: Must SIGINT or SIGTERM be received after the boundary, or is `SERVED` also chosen when the signal is received before the boundary but stops the server only after the boundary?

quotes:
SERVED, value `served`: after it, a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends
judgement.why: SERVED depends on the signal stopping the web server after the boundary, not on when the signal was first received.

questions: How must code decide that SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped the server when a signal overlaps a shutdown that was already requested or underway?

judgement.why: No passage establishes an internal graceful-shutdown action or a history in which such an action overlaps a signal, so the proposed causal-attribution witness cannot be built from the texts.
